title: OpenAI Error Envelope (hermes-auto-router wire subset, v1)
description: The error body an OpenAI-compatible provider returns on a non-2xx response to POST /v1/chat/completions, and the body the gateway relays back unchanged. This is a different shape from chat.completion: it carries no id, object, created, model, or choices, so openai-chat-response.v1 does not describe it and error bodies were previously unvalidated. design.md 20.3 lists context-length errors in the contract-test set; 401 invalid-api-key and 429 rate-limit bodies use the same envelope. This is a RELAY schema: additionalProperties is true at both levels because providers add fields the gateway must forward verbatim, and a closed object here would reject traffic the gateway is required to pass through. The typed properties below bound the SHAPE of the fields this schema names; they do not constrain what a provider chooses to put in them, and they say nothing about fields a provider adds that are not named here.

errorDetail.description: The error detail object. message and type are the two fields every OpenAI-compatible provider observed so far sets on every error response, so they are required; param and code are frequently absent or explicitly null and are therefore optional and nullable.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong, as written by the provider. Free text of provider-chosen length. The gateway relays it; it does not parse, truncate, or interpret it, and nothing here bounds what a provider includes in it.

type.description: Provider error category, such as invalid_request_error, authentication_error, or rate_limit_error. Deliberately not an enum: the value set is provider-defined and grows, and an enum here would reject an error the gateway must still relay.

param.description: The request parameter the error refers to, such as 'messages' or 'max_tokens'. Null when the error is not attributable to one parameter.

code.description: Machine-readable error code, such as context_length_exceeded or invalid_api_key. Null when the provider does not supply one. Integer is permitted because some OpenAI-compatible relays put the HTTP status here (code: 429) rather than a string slug; such a body is one the gateway relays byte-for-byte, and typing this field ['string','null'] made a contract test reject traffic the gateway is required to pass through -- the exact closure this schema's own description warns against. Widened, not removed: a code that is neither string, integer nor null is still a violation.
